newsitem.title: UK: Frothy cocoa gets a kick from late short covering.
newsitem.headline: Frothy cocoa gets a kick from late short covering.

text.p: Cocoa flexed its muscle again in late dealings on Friday, overcoming initial technical hurdles and paving the way for further gains next week, traders said.
The benchmark May contract was jolted out of an initial consolidative mood by a fresh spell of short covering that carried it to an intraday high of 949 stg a tonne, the highest since December 12.
"It's mainly local jobbers. They were holding shorts and they began to cover after lack of follow through on the downside," said one trader, referring to a session low of 931 stg on May.

The May position pared gains at the finish, but it was still 14 stg higher on the day at a technically inspiring 946 stg, clearing Wednesday's peak of 945. The weekly gains totalled 59 stg or nearly seven percent.
Most other forward contracts recorded similar gains, but the far end of the board was weaker, also because some distant contracts absorbed origin offers.

Turnover on the day totalled 7,664 lots and the day's heavy switch trade continued to indicate a tightening structure. These included May/Dec trading at 26 stg, May/July at 11, July/Sept 11 and May/March crossed at 45.
Friday's last-minute jump supported views about the market's upward aspirations, which also boded well with an improving technical outlook.
"It may have to range sideways to go a little bit further...I would have said it's got a good chance of breaking upwards," said Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis.

But manufacturers were yet to be convinced of the technically-led rally, which has so far totalled 84 stg in two weeks, and continued to be relaxed about forward cover given abundant supplies in the physical market.
"Europe is swamped with cocoa," said one.

Some traders reckon without the backing of manufacturers and a change in the fundamental picture, which remains oversupplied after another apparently big Ivorian harvest, the rally may run out of steam.
Having climbed above 945, the May contract is now braced for a run towards the December peak of 972 but may encounter some resistance at 960.
